answer: An agent may bind its signing key to only one factory-fused secure-boot kernel, a scarce serialized chip nobody can photocopy. Peers enroll the operator by challenging that kernel for a fresh attestation quote and recomputing it against the vendor fuse map; a second key on the same serial burns the posted bond. To block remote clones, the kernel must reply from a licensed coastal island cable landing whose delay is cross-checked by a highland summit clock. Each extra identity therefore demands another fused chip and another landing concession, so the attacker's bill grows at least linearly.
